## Proposed change

The aim of this PR is to reset Unifi bandwidth sensor to 0 when a client disconnect is detected through the heartbeat mechanism.
Currently bandwidth sensors keep the last value before disconnect, which corrupts graphs and statistics.

This is an alternate implementation to #104459 based on heartbeats instead of events, as discussed with code owner in the linked issue.

issue_context.title: Unifi bandwidth sensor doesn't reset to zero on client disconnect
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hello,

I noticed that Unifi bandwidth sensors do not reset to 0 when a client disconnects from the network.
Home assistant then considers the last value before the disconnect as the current, valid one.
This leads to incorrect graphs, statistics etc, especially for wireless clients which disconnect often.
Currently as a workaround I use template sensors which combine bandwidth sensors and presence detection to set the value to 0, but this is cumbersome.
I think the Unifi integration should reset the bandwidth sensors (both TX and RX) when a client is disconnected.

I researched the code a bit and have thought of 2 possible fixes :
- subscribe bandwidth sensors to disconnect events and reset the sensors when these events fire
- or have some sort of polling/timer to reset a bandwidth sensor if it is not updated for a predefined time
If you think this could work I would be happy to look into the code and hopefully provide a PR.

Best,

![Screenshot from 2023-10-14 19-02-10](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/21991867/4a150d13-58be-4ab6-91aa-f3281bdb749e)

review_comments:
I think this falls under calculating state which we don't allow for integrations that integrate devices or services.

The library should handle this if needed.

This is the same logic as how the device tracker calculates availability so there is nothing new introduced with this PR

I don't want any smart things happening in the library, it should just represent the data

I don't follow. We're not allowed to directly set a state with a made up value that doesn't come directly from the API library. If this isn't possible the state or entity should not be included in the integration.

If the device is away then UniFi won't send any more data, it will never say that it is 0.

I guess the alternative is to mark the entity unavailable.
If the entity represents a feature of a device and that device isn't connected we normally mark the entity as unavailable, yes.
Hello, let me know if I should create a new PR.
If marking the entity as unavailable on device disconnection sounds good, please make a PR for that.
You can simplify this as the device tracker logic is about figuring out if the client is at home or not, where as here you only want to care if no new data has been sent for a given time
I have removed all ssid logic, keeping only the last_seen check
